headline: Forum Where Everyone Pretends It's Still 2007 Celebrates 17 Years of Denial
subheadline: Members maintain elaborate fiction; iPhone still considered 'overhyped'
summary: An online community has spent 17 years maintaining the collective fiction that time stopped in 2007.
content:
The web forum Eternal2007.net is celebrating what members call their "first anniversary"—for the 17th consecutive year—as the community maintains its commitment to pretending the year 2007 never ended.

The forum, which has operated continuously since 2007, requires all members to roleplay as if current events haven't happened. Discussions center on whether the iPhone will succeed ("overhyped"), speculation about the upcoming Obama vs. Clinton primary ("too close to call"), and recommendations for the best Myspace layouts.

"Happy 2007 everyone!" reads a recent post. "Can you believe this year? The last Harry Potter book is coming out. Spider-Man 3 looks promising. What a time to be alive."

New members must pass a "temporal purity test" demonstrating knowledge of 2007 culture and commit to never acknowledging anything that happened after December 31, 2007. References to subsequent years result in immediate banning.

"We had someone mention 'TikTok' last month," said administrator @Forever07. "Permabanned. We don't know what that is and we don't want to know."

The community has developed elaborate workarounds for modern necessities. Members discuss "the internet" but only reference websites that existed in 2007. They share music but only albums released before the cutoff. One member asked for computer help and received advice to "upgrade to Windows Vista."

Psychologists have studied the forum as an example of collective escapism. "They've created a shared reality," noted one researcher. "And honestly? 2007 wasn't bad. I understand the appeal."

Membership has grown steadily, now reaching 8,470 active users. When asked why people join, @Forever07 responded: "Have you seen what's happened since 2007? People are exhausted. We offer an alternative."

At press time, the forum was hotly debating whether Britney Spears would recover from her "rough patch."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
